Micah Lasher's $3.3M raised and $10.8M in outside support dwarf Caroline Shinkle's $155K

model.rationale: A D+33 district, Lasher's overwhelming financial advantage over Shinkle, and market pricing at 97% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite Jerry Nadler's retirement; the only real question is the size of the margin.
model.watch: Turnout in a low-profile open-seat race could move the margin by several points, though not plausibly the winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 12th District is among the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+33. Jerry Nadler's retirement opens the seat, but Democrats remain heavily favored to hold it. Micah Lasher has raised $3.3 million and drawn more than $10.7 million in outside support, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised about $155,000. Two independent candidates trail far behind in fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and market pricing. Polymarket puts the Democratic candidate's win chance at 97 percent. The expected margin is roughly 29 points, meaning the main question is the size of the win rather than the winner. A Republican upset would require a swing far beyond anything seen in recent cycles in this New York City district.
